q: The Squire transformation for linearised Navier-Stokes shows that 3D instabilities can be reduced to 2D instabilities. More precisely:
opts: All 3D instabilities are equivalent to 2D instabilities
Any 3D normal mode (k_x, k_y, k_z) instability corresponds to a 2D instability at the same Reynolds number (Squire's theorem)
exp: Squire's theorem: for any unstable 3D oblique mode at Reynolds number Re, there is a more unstable 2D mode at a lower Re'. Therefore the critical Reynolds number for instability is determined by 2D disturbances (the Orr-Sommerfeld equation).
